triples.head: RNA polymerase I
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase I synthesizes all of the rRNAs from the tandemly duplicated set of 18S, 5.8S, and 28S ribosomal genes.

triples.head: RNA polymerase II
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase II is located in the nucleus and synthesizes all protein-coding nuclear pre-mRNAs.

triples.head: RNA polymerase III
triples.tail: 5S rRNA, tRNAs, and small nuclear RNAs
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase III is also located in the nucleus. This polymerase transcribes a variety of structural RNAs that includes the 5S pre-rRNA, transfer pre-RNAs (pre-tRNAs), and small nuclear pre-RNAs.

triples.head: RNA polymerase I
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase I is completely insensitive to α-amanitin, meaning that the polymerase can transcribe DNA in vitro in the presence of this poison.

triples.head: RNA polymerase II
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase II is extremely sensitive to α-amanitin. The toxin prevents the enzyme from progressing down the DNA, and thus inhibits transcription.

triples.head: RNA polymerase III
triples.evidence: RNA polymerase III is moderately sensitive to the toxin.
